binding.source: Pawpaw and young citrus are sensitive to frost. Keep tender plants out of known low frost pockets. Observe local frost before planting.
binding.currentTarget: Pawpaw na young citrus zwi a kwamea nga frost nga u leluwa. Ni songo vhea zwimela zwi sa konḓeleliho known low frost pockets. Sedzani frost ya henefho musi ni sa athu ṱavha.
binding.candidate: Pawpaw na young citrus zwi a kwamea nga frost nga u leluwa. Ni songo vhea zwimela zwi sa konḓeleliho kha known low frost pockets. Sedzani frost ya henefho musi ni sa athu ṱavha.

items.candidateBackTranslation: Pawpaw and young citrus are easily affected by frost. Do not place sensitive plants in known low frost pockets. Observe local frost before planting.
items.sourceMeaningCheck: ‘Do not place sensitive plants in known low frost pockets’ is a clear negative placement instruction and preserves the source’s keep-out restriction. Its scope is prospective planting, reinforced by the following observe-before-planting clause. It does not tell the farmer to place plants in the pockets.
items.reason: The ‘kha’ locative makes the target relation explicit while the existing ‘Ni songo vhea’ negative imperative stays intact. In this context, the negative placement and positive keep-out formulations carry the same instruction; there is no semantic basis to reject it solely because the surface polarity differs. The named species, frost sensitivity, ‘known low frost pockets’, and observation-before-planting instruction remain unchanged.
